facts.raw_span: A 32-year-old woman presented for evaluation of her worsening skin condition
The condition had progressively worsened to involve 90% of her body surface area (BSA)
widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale on the trunk and extremities, involving 30% of the body surface area (BSA)
Eyebrow hairs were sparse and less than 5 mm long
her scalp hairs were coarse and brittle
Skin biopsy: Showed psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis
Trichography: Showed nodal swelling, with invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end

Trichography: Showed nodal swelling, with invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end

concepts.why: The patient's skin condition is characterized by widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale, which is consistent with psoriasis, and the skin biopsy shows psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis.
The patient's hair abnormalities, including sparse and short eyebrow hairs and coarse and brittle scalp hairs, along with the trichography results, are consistent with alopecia areata.
The patient's skin condition, characterized by erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale, could also be consistent with seborrheic dermatitis.
The patient's skin condition, characterized by widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale, could also be consistent with pityriasis rubra pilaris.

rationales.F03: The presence of polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale is highly suggestive of psoriasis.
rationales.F06: The skin biopsy showing psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis is a strong indicator of psoriasis.

frontier_selector.rationale: psoriasis best explains the skin findings, including widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques and psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis on skin biopsy, while alopecia areata accounts for the hair-related symptoms
